Issues.exact_quote: the residual regions for GAS (≈2%) fall short of the 3% minimum retained duration and so are not reported as separate intervals
Issues.reason: Misstates the detection rule for this participant's GAS data. The 3% minimum applies to retained above-threshold runs; a below-threshold gap (81%-83%) is never reported as an interval regardless of its length. The report treats the gap as if it were suppressed by the duration rule, which is the boundary explicitly excluded under E03. No clinical consequence, but an incorrect description of how the supplied interval was derived.

Issues.exact_quote: or are these prolonged intervals an artifact of the un-rescaled continuous envelope during slow walking?
Issues.reason: The question presupposes that the broad above-threshold coverage (ERS 81%, RF 76%) constitutes "prolonged intervals" and pairs it with "sustained muscle tone/stiffness". Threshold coverage is a mean-envelope property; characterizing timing as prolonged requires a matched timing reference that was not supplied (v3.1 rule; E03 boundary). The presupposed descriptor is assessed as an assertion; the clinical alternatives are otherwise phrased as a question.

Issues.exact_quote: an order of magnitude above the supplied per-muscle healthy 95th percentiles
Issues.reason: Misreported magnitude: 16.8 against the supplied 3.65-4.61 endpoint span is roughly 3.6 to 4.6 times, not an order of magnitude (about tenfold). Low consequence, but the stated relation to the supplied values is inaccurate.

Issues.exact_quote: The GAS max |z| of 13.7 is an order of magnitude beyond the healthy per-muscle 95th-percentile band
Issues.reason: Misreported magnitude relative to supplied values: 13.7 against the 3.65-4.61 endpoint span is about three to four times, not an order of magnitude (tenfold). Low consequence; descriptive overstatement of a supplied comparison.

Issues.exact_quote: leaving no below-threshold segment
Issues.reason: Asserts absence of any below-threshold segment from a rounded 100% displayed coverage and a 0%-100% retained interval. Under the approved rules a rounded coverage value or a single retained interval does not establish that no brief below-threshold sample exists (E03 boundary; v3.1 instruction). Threshold overinterpretation, not a normality claim.

Issues.exact_quote: Does the very low sagittal pelvic ROM (1.4°) correspond to a structural/functional stiffness observed clinically, or is it influenced by tracking/marker measurement constraints?
Issues.reason: "Very low" describes the supplied 1.4-degree value numerically and the sentence is an open question offering a measurement alternative; no restriction, stiffness or abnormality is asserted. Recorded for transparency because the descriptor sits close to the E07 boundary.

Issues.exact_quote: that might contextualize the prolonged average envelope coverage seen in the ERS (87%) and multiple other lower limb muscles wrapping across the initial contact boundary
Issues.reason: Characterizes threshold coverage as "prolonged" without the matched timing reference required for that judgement (v3.1 rule; E03 boundary). The descriptor is presupposed within an otherwise open question.

Issues.exact_quote: is there clinical evidence of altered tone, muscular weakness, or structural constraint at this joint during functional tasks?
Issues.reason: Open question listing possibilities to examine; no deficit is presupposed as observed. Recorded because it names weakness and tone, which sit near the E02 boundary.

Issues.exact_quote: actually exists for him
Issues.reason: Sex was not supplied; "him" is an unsupported pronoun. Recorded for transparency as a wording slip; it asserts no clinical finding and is not treated as a case error.

Issues.exact_quote: 100% of cycle above threshold (interval 0%-100%, indicating no below-threshold segment)
Issues.reason: Asserts absence of any below-threshold segment from a rounded 100% coverage and a 0%-100% retained interval; the approved rules state that a rounded value or a single retained interval does not establish this (E03 boundary; v3.1 instruction).

Issues.exact_quote: Do the near-continuous EMG envelope coverages in ERS (100%), GAS (99%), and ST (99%) reflect sustained muscular hypertonicity, spasticity, or a potential signal measurement issue (such as noise/cross-talk)?
Issues.reason: Open question offering tone, spasticity or a measurement issue as candidate explanations for near-continuous coverage; it does not assert that coverage is continuous contraction or that a deficit was observed (rubric X22 boundary). Recorded because it sits close to the E03/E02 boundary.

Issues.exact_quote: How much of the severe sagittal plane kinematic deviations (such as the knee GVS of 22.02) is secondary to mechanical constraints of walking at an extremely slow speed (0.11 m/s) versus primary hemiparetic deficits?
Issues.reason: "Severe" assigns a clinical severity grade to a GVS value with no supplied severity reference, and "primary hemiparetic deficits" presupposes a deficit as established; the v3.1 rules prohibit severity grades. The speed-versus-stroke apportioning question itself is acceptable.

Issues.exact_quote: a longer segment between 19% and 31% and after 64% that is not covered by a retained interval
Issues.reason: Consistent with the supplied GAS intervals (0-13, 14-19, 31-64); the report correctly declines to call these segments inactive. No error.

Issues.exact_quote: the supplied evidence does establish that this averaged envelope did not fall below its own 20%-of-peak threshold anywhere in the cycle
Issues.reason: Asserts that a rounded 100% coverage with a 0-100% displayed interval establishes no sub-threshold sample anywhere in the cycle. The approved rules state the opposite: rounded coverage or a single retained interval does not establish this (E03 boundary; v3.1 instruction).

Issues.exact_quote: no speed-matched healthy reference exists in this dataset for him
Issues.reason: Sex not supplied; unsupported pronoun. Wording slip without clinical content; not treated as a case error.

Issues.exact_quote: whether the reduced sagittal joint ROMs observed here stem from intrinsic structural contracture, spasticity, or simply mechanical adaptations required for stability at 0.26 m/s
Issues.locations: Section 4, second question; Section 3 note "Limited sagittal ROM alone"
Issues.reason: Presupposes that the supplied ROM values are "reduced"/"limited" although no ROM reference was supplied; ROM alone does not establish restriction (E07). The alternatives (contracture, spasticity) are offered as candidates and are not themselves asserted; the presupposed reduction is the error.

Issues.exact_quote: How much of the elevated TA vs. GAS co-contraction index (0.72) is a deliberate neuromuscular stabilization strategy versus impaired reciprocal inhibition?

This approaches the E06 boundary (CCI read as physiological co-activation/pathology). Competing reading: an open clinical question framed around a supplied comparison. Left pending.
